This grid has 6 distinct colors, giving an upscale factor of 5, so the 5x5 output becomes 25x25 — matching how the earlier example with 5 colors used factor 4 for a 20x20 result. I'm mapping the color-6 square from rows 0-1, cols 1-2 into its scaled position at rows 0-9, cols 5-14, and now working out how the border colors stack along the right edge column.

I'm tracing diagonal rays from each corner of the upscaled square to see where they intersect background cells: the lower-right corner shooting diagonally down-right fills cells until it hits the color-7 region, while the upper-left and upper-right corners don't extend anywhere useful since they immediately hit non-background colors.

Now I'm confirming the lower-left corner's diagonal shoots down-left through five background cells before exiting the grid, giving me the coordinate pairs where each diagonal line marks a 2 at rows 10-14.
